questions.question: A quadratic Bézier at t = 0.5: point A is halfway from P₀ to P₁, and point B is halfway from P₁ to P₂. Where is the curve point?
An axe returns along a quadratic Bézier curve. You move its middle handle upward but leave the start and hand positions fixed. What happens to the path?
answers: It passes through the handle at t = 0.5
It bends toward the handle; its ends stay put
Its end moves up with the handle
It stays the same; handles only change speed

questions.question: A curve component computes power-basis coefficients C₀, C₁, C₂ once in Start() and draws its line from them. In Play mode you drag the middle handle. What does the line do?
answers: Follows the handle; all three forms agree
Follows the handle with uneven spacing
Keeps its old shape until recomputed

questions.question: A recall path starts at the stuck axe (P₀), bows out through a side handle (P₁), and ends at the hand (P₂). At t = 0, which way is the axe moving?
A follower takes equal steps in t at equal time intervals. Its sampled positions are crowded together in one part of the path. How does it move through that part?
answers: It depends on frame rate, not spacing
Faster than where samples spread out
Slower than where samples spread out
Same speed; only the line looks uneven

questions.question: You switch the recall from a quadratic to a cubic Bézier. What does the extra handle let you control?
answers: A point the path must pass through

questions.question: Recall begins while the axe is still flying under a dynamic Rigidbody. Before the recall loop starts setting its position along the curve, what should happen to the Rigidbody?
You spin the axe during recall. It reaches the hand, but it sits there at a crooked angle. What did the catch skip?
answers: Reparenting the axe to the hand
